question.leadin: This man used Zacuto's charts to predict a February 1504 eclipse in Jamaica.
question.text: Name this Genoese explorer who left Spain for the New World in 1492.
question.clue: His rivals included a subordinate on his first trip, Martin Pinzon, as well as Francisco de Babadilla who arrested him and his brothers Bartholemew and Diego for mismanagement of the newly founded La Isabela.

swap.leadin: This conflict saw the formation of volunteer International Brigades to fight fascists as well as the bombing of Guernica by the German Condor Legion.
swap.text: Name this 1936 to 1939 war in which Nationalist forces rebelled against the government of President Manuel Azana.
swap.clue: A volunteer unit primarily comprising Americans in this conflict was the Abraham Lincoln Brigade, which fought with the Republicans.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Counter-Reformation.
question.text: This institution of the Counter-Reformation, whose first chief was Tomas de Torquemada, was established by Isabella I of Castile to root out Moriscos, Jews, and non-Catholics.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Inquisition [or Tribunal of the Holy Office of the Inquisition]
question.clue: This organization forced people to wear yellow sackcloths called sanbenito at public auto-da-fe's put on by its first leader Tomas de Torquemada.

swap.text: Moriscos were forced out of Spain if they didn't convert after the end of this hundreds-year-long conflict of Christian kingdoms against taifas. It ended with the fall of Granada in 1492.
swap.clue: During this period, the corpse of El Cid was placed on a horse to boost the morale of troops in the defense of Valencia.

question.leadin: One of this ruler's major reforms was establishing the Santa Hermandad to combat crime.
question.text: Name this queen of Castile who agreed to finance Christopher Columbus' trips to the New World. Her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon set the stage for a unified Spain.
question.clue: This ruler was often advised by Tomas de Torquemada, who headed an institution set up by this monarch and her husband which often conducted auto-da-fe ceremonies.

swap.leadin: This man became the leader of his party after the Siege of Alcazar.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Falange and generalissimo of the Nationalists who was succeeded by Juan Carlos I.
swap.clue: He responded to the communist-backed "Red Terror" by initiating the "White Terror," which lasted into his reign.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a period in European history.
question.text: This state was the last Muslim emirate on the Iberian peninsula, following the collapse of the Almohad dynasty after the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa. It was conquered by Castile in 1492 after its leader Bobadil agreed to surrender it.
question.clue: A fortified complex in this polity's namesake city was beautified by Yusuf I, whose successor built the Court of the Lions.

swap.text: The Sicilian Vespers happened concurrently with a crusade named after this region. A ruler of this Spanish region issued the Alhambra Decree and married Germaine de Foix.
swap.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

question.leadin: Give these terms from the rule of Napoleon.
question.text: Known as War of Independence by native Spaniards, this attempt to subjugate Portugal and Spain lasted from 1808 to 1814.

swap.text: After the arrest of its leaders Mikel Albizu and Harriet Aguirre, it proclaimed a permanent ceasefire in March 2006. For 15 points, name this militant group active in Spain, whose name is an acronym translating to "Basque Fatherland and Liberty."
swap.clue: This group's political wing was the Herri Batasuna.

question.text: Members of this ethnic group were particularly active in the whaling industry, setting up a fishing village at Red Bay in Labrador. Whalers from this ethnic group were killed in a 1615 massacre perpetrated by locals in Iceland.
question.clue: This ethnic group's whaling activities led to the creation of a pidgin described by Jon Olafsson, and 32 shipwrecked members of this ethnic group were murdered in Iceland in the 1615 "Slaying of the Spaniards."

swap.text: This 1212 battle was a huge defeat for the Almohads in Andalusia at the hands of various Christian Iberian kingdoms. It set in motion a process that, by the end of the century, reduced Muslim presence in Spain to basically just Granada.
swap.answer: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
swap.clue: Innocent III convinced some veterans of the Fourth Crusade to campaign with the winning side in this battle, whose commanders included Sancho VII of Navarre.

question.leadin: John II offered people affected by this law asylum before deporting many to Sao Tome. but his son Manuel I was pressured into replicating the edict 5 years later.
question.text: Name this law, passed under the pretense of protecting conversos from subversion, which led migrants to settle in Mizrahi communities in Morocco and Algeria.
question.clue: The most famous such incident took place in Spain in 1492 through a decree named for this Muslim fort in Andalusia, one of the final holdouts to Ferdinand and Isabella.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Jose Sanjurjo.
swap.text: Both Sanjurjo and this fellow general died in plane crashes, leaving Franco as the sole Nationalist leader. This man coined the term "fifth column" during the siege of Madrid.
swap.clue: Although they were nominally led by Jose Sanjurjo, this man was the true leader of the Nationalist forces. After his sudden death in 1937, Franco would become their leader:

question.leadin: In November 2014, Spanish prosecutors announced charges against Artur Mas for illegally conducting a referendum on this question.
question.text: Identify this cause which seeks to make Barcelona the capital of a new country.
question.clue: The paramilitary Terra Lliure ("LEEW-ruh") and the ERC party both support this cause, whose "refoundation" was led by Artur Mas.

swap.leadin: This man led Spanish troops to force Portugal to cease trade with Britain as part of a Franco-Spanish alliance in the brief War of the Oranges.
swap.text: Name this "Prince of the Peace", a powerful prime minister under Charles IV.
swap.clue: He became his country's first commander to adopt the title of generalisimo while leading troops in the War of the Oranges.

question.text: The namesake of Gibraltar, Tariq ibn Ziyad, ensured the Islamic conquest of Spain by leading the force that won this decisive 711 battle against Visigoths under Roderic.
question.answerHtml: The Battle of Guadalete [also accept the Battle of Jerez de la Frontera; La Janda; Rio Barbate; or the Transducine Promontories]
question.clue: Muslim forces led by Berber Tariq overthrew the last Visigothic king of Spain, Roderick at this A.D. 711 battle named for the river where it was fought.

swap.leadin: This man died after stepping on a landmine in the First Indochina War.
swap.text: Name this Hungarian photographer who is credited with photographing a dying militiaman in a work known as Falling Soldier. That work's true origins have been long disputed.
swap.clue: The "Falling Soldier" photograph showing the moment immediately after the death of a Spanish Civil War soldier was made by this Hungarian photojournalist who covered several early 20th century conflicts. He died after stepping on a mine in French Indochina.

question.leadin: This concept is defined as "life, borne by living societies founded in its name" in French historian Pierre Nora's work on its "sites," or lieux.
question.text: Identify this concept that names a 2007 law that banned Francoists from rallying at the Valley of the Fallen, in a reversal of a 1970s "pact" named for the opposite of this concept.
question.answerHtml: memory [or mémoire; or memoria; accept word forms of remembering; accept lieu de mémoire; accept Historical Memory Law]
